title: Intraperitoneal Glucose Tolerance Test in Mice
author: Henri Brunengraber
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ydtfs6n
materials: Weigh each mouse and record weight.

steps.title: Fast mice and prepare cages
steps.instruction: Fast mice overnight or for 6 hours; at 5:00 PM remove each mouse from its home cage and place it into a clean cage containing water but no food.

steps.title: Begin GTT day
steps.instruction: On the following day, start the glucose tolerance test by 9:00 AM.

steps.title: Prepare glucometer
steps.instruction: Insert a glucose test strip into the glucometer and verify that the strip code matches the strip type being used.

steps.title: Collect fasting blood glucose
steps.instruction: Snip the mouse tail, place a drop of blood onto the glucose strip already in the glucometer, record the fasting glucose as time 0, then dip the tail into clotisol to clot the blood.

steps.title: Calculate glucose injection volume
steps.instruction: Calculate the volume of glucose solution required to deliver 2 g glucose per kg body weight for each mouse and record the calculated volume.

steps.title: Inject glucose intraperitoneally
steps.instruction: Inject each mouse intraperitoneally with the calculated glucose volume, spacing injections 3 minutes apart; this marks time 0.

steps.title: Measure glucose at time points
steps.instruction: At 15 minutes, 30 minutes, 60 minutes, and 120 minutes after the glucose injection, repeat the fasting blood glucose collection (snip tail, apply blood to strip, record glucose).

steps.title: Insulin measurement note
steps.instruction: Do not collect extra blood for insulin measurements from these mice; instead use a separate group of mice for insulin sampling after glucose injection.
